subject: Post-call: LeadStream PoC readiness & success metrics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@leadstream.ai>, Marco Giannini <marco@leadstream.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: LeadStream PoC readiness & success metrics

Hi Elena / Marco —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single checklist for the PoC kickoff. I focused this on measurable acceptance criteria so we can make a go/no-go decision at the end of the 3-week trial.

Summary of goals we heard from you:
- Replace your current summarization microservice with a hosted Redwood endpoint.
- Meet stricter latency for interactive workflows (search + summarize).
- Keep per-token cost under a target to preserve unit economics for production.
- Demonstrate no major quality regressions vs. your current baseline (human ratings).

Proposed PoC scope / timeline:
- Duration: 3 weeks (trial window recommended: Aug 10 — Aug 31)
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): infra prep, API keys, sample dataset, network allowlist
- Week 1: integration + smoke tests, baseline run using your 1k test prompts
- Week 2: full run (load + quality), real traffic simulation, perf profiling
- Week 3: quality review, cost analysis, final readout

Proposed success criteria (quantifiable):
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 150 ms for 512-token requests under steady-state load
- Throughput: sustained 50 requests/sec with <=10% tail latency increase
- Cost: average token cost <= $0.0008/token across the test set (including batching effects)
- Quality: automated semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) >= 0.85 vs. baseline summaries AND human rating mean >= 4/5 on a 200-sample set
- Hallucination: <2% critical hallucination incidents on the sampled set

Ownership (suggested):
- LeadStream technical owner: Marco Giannini (integration + data sampling)
- Redwood SE lead: Ben Carter (integration support, metric collection)
- Redwood ML lead: Dylan Brooks (quality measurement + perf tuning)
- Customer success: Marissa Cole (readout, SOW alignment)

Attachments I will send after this note: PoC checklist and a fillable template for expected test prompts / sample size.

Next steps I propose before Aug 6:
1) Marco to confirm network allowlist and test dataset availability (reply with S3 link or sample CSV)
2) LeadStream to sign the PoC addendum (DocuSign link below) if you want Redwood-managed credits for the 3-week test
3) Redwood to provision a test endpoint and share credentials by Aug 9

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign?token=abc123-leadstream
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/companies/67890

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: LeadStream_PoC_Template.xlsx (Excel)

From: Marco Giannini <marco@leadstream.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@leadstream.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: LeadStream PoC readiness & success metrics

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. We like the concrete KPIs. Quick answers from my side: 
- We can make a 1k-sample CSV available by Aug 6 (I'll share an S3 presigned link).
- Network: our infra team will need the Redwood egress ranges and a quick diagram of which endpoints we call. I'll attach a short network diagram tomorrow.
- DocuSign: Elena will handle approvals; we should be able to sign the PoC addendum by Aug 7.

Two clarifying questions on metrics: 
1) For the cost metric, do you assume tokenization on our side or on Redwood's? We want the figure to match our billing model.
2) For throughput, could you confirm whether 50 req/sec assumes batching at the client or server-side batching? We may need to emulate client batching to match production.

Also — can you surface any model variants you plan to test? We prefer to try a smaller quantized variant first if it helps cost.

Thanks,
Marco
Marco Giannini
Senior Platform Engineer, LeadStream
Attachment: network_blocking_diagram.pdf (PDF)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marco Giannini <marco@leadstream.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena@leadstream.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2026 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: LeadStream PoC readiness & success metrics

Marco — good questions. Short answers: 
- Cost calc: Redwood will calculate token cost server-side (tokens consumed by the model). We will provide a cost breakdown in the week-3 analysis and include guidance for mapping to client-side tokenization if you need it.
- Throughput: the 50 req/sec target assumes server-side continuous batching with per-request latency SLOs; we'll emulate your client batching pattern in the load harness if you share it.
- Model variants: plan is to test two variants: a quantized 8-bit-friendly model for cost-first runs and the full FP16 variant for quality runs. Dylan will tune batching/kv cache parameters between runs.

Updated acceptance checklist (minor edits):
- Latency: p95 <= 150 ms @ 512 tokens (server-side measurement)
- Throughput: sustain 50 req/sec for 10 minute windows with <=10% p95 increase
- Cost: server-side average <= $0.0008/token across test dataset (we will show per-batch breakdown)
- Quality: embedding cosine >= 0.85 vs baseline OR human mean >= 4/5 on 200 samples
- Observability: Redwood to provide per-request tracing and token-level cost logs for the trial window

I'll attach a populated PoC template (small example filled) by EOD. If that looks good, we'll schedule the provisioning window Aug 9.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Marissa / Karthik / Dylan — internal note after Marco's reply and signatures:
- Marco will provide S3 link for samples by EOD Aug 6 and their infra diagram (he already sent a brief network PDF).
- Elena will sign the DocuSign by Aug 7; once signed we can spin up the endpoint on Aug 9.
- Action items: 
  - Dylan: prepare quality evaluation harness (embedding comparator, 200-sample human queue) and perf baseline scripts. Target: have harness ready by Aug 8.
  - Marissa: prepare the readout deck template and cost comparison slide; coordinate customer-facing scheduling for Aug 31 readout.
  - Karthik: confirm SOW language on PoC credits and capture any commercial ask if they push for extended trial.

I'll provision test endpoint credentials on Aug 9 and drop into the HubSpot record. Keeping this thread as the single source of truth.

Ben
